Rishi — attaching the artifacts requested. Quick notes inline.

Attachments:
- redwood_kms_rotation_log_2025-2026.csv (CSV export from our audit pipeline; columns: timestamp, key_id, action, actor, previous_key_version, new_key_version)
- hsm_attestation_letter_2026-03.pdf (vendor-signed attestation; covers FIPS 140-2 L3 modules used for key material)
- kms_access_review_summary_q2_2026.pdf (executive summary of quarterly access review)
- kms_key_policy_screenshot.png (policy view showing "no-export" flag on customer-managed keys)

Short answers you can paste into the reply to Jordan:
1) Rotation cadence: Platform-managed RSA/AES keys are rotated on a 12-month schedule by default; some keys (short-lived ephemeral wrapping keys) rotate hourly. Rotation events and principals are logged in the attached CSV.
2) HSM: We use a cloud HSM provider with FIPS 140-2/3 L3 certified modules (see attestation). Customer key material for "customer-managed" keys is generated and wrapped inside the HSM; private key material is not exportable in plaintext.
3) Access reviews: The attached PDF contains the list of roles with KMS access and the last review date (2026-05-15). Role separation is enforced (infra-admin vs sec-admin) and service accounts are audited monthly.
4) Key export policy: Customer-managed keys have a "no-export" policy by default. We support BYOK via an import/wrapping flow where keys are wrapped and stored in HSM-backed envelopes; raw key material is never stored in plaintext outside HSM.

Storage: Full artifacts are staged in a customer-specific S3 bucket (read-only link below). I flagged the CSV to remove full principal email addresses and replaced with role tokens per Jordan's usual requirements; we kept the actor field but masked personal emails.

S3 link (read-only): https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-evidence/heliumai/rotation_log_2025-2026.csv

If you want, I can also export a limited audit trail showing just HeliumAI-related key ids.

— Monica
